directions.title: Why Microservices Ditch REST for gRPC
directions.audienceProblem: REST with JSON is slow and connection-heavy across hundreds of internal microservice calls.
directions.tensionHook: Why do high-scale microservices ditch REST and JSON for gRPC?
directions.promise: See the two architectural bottlenecks gRPC eliminates inside backend systems.
directions.payoff: Binary Protobuf plus single multiplexed HTTP/2 connection unlocks massive speed and type safety.
directions.visualApproach: Animated comparison of JSON string bloat vs compact Protobuf schema, and HTTP/1.1 sequential requests vs single-socket HTTP/2 stream multiplexing.

directions.title: The Hidden CPU Cost of JSON
directions.audienceProblem: Microservices burn CPU parsing text strings instead of executing business logic.
directions.tensionHook: Your microservices are burning CPU just reading text.
directions.promise: Compare byte-for-byte serialization speed between JSON and Protobuf.
directions.payoff: Protobuf replaces string keys with compact binary field tags and strict schemas.
directions.visualApproach: Byte breakdown comparing identical payload in JSON vs Protobuf.
risks: Focuses only on serialization, omitting HTTP/2 transport benefits

directions.title: Stop Opening 100 TCP Connections
directions.audienceProblem: Traditional REST APIs suffer from connection overhead and head-of-line blocking under load.
directions.tensionHook: Opening a new connection for every request is killing your cluster.
directions.promise: Visualize how HTTP/2 multiplexing handles parallel streams over one socket.
directions.payoff: One persistent socket with native bidirectional streaming across services.
directions.visualApproach: Network pipeline visualization of concurrent frames over one connection.
risks: Omits the type-safety and compact payload benefits of Protocol Buffers
